title: Parallel reading lab
subtitle: Compare grammatical choices without collapsing distinct texts.
overview: Parallel passages can sharpen observation: compare wording, verb forms, and paragraph placement after each text has first been read independently.
A comparison notes sameness and difference. It does not automatically turn one author’s wording into the other’s.

sections.title: Compare the Greek wording
rows: Compare the forms of address: “child” and “man.”
Compare the verbal form and word order.
Compare Mark’s present narrative form with Luke’s aorist form.

items.grc: ἄνθρωπε, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου.
items.en: Luke: “Man, your sins have been forgiven.”
